title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 6th Proof The Testimony Of The Purified Ones Scholars And Sages

questions.question: What kind of people are mentioned at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: They are many sincere, purified, careful scholars and faithful wise people.

questions.question: How did these scholars and sages reach very high levels of learning?
questions.answer: They reached it through the teachings and instruction brought by the Prophet.

questions.question: What surprising fact about the Prophet is highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: He was not taught reading and writing, yet great knowledge came through him.

questions.question: Besides sacred truths, what two other things does the passage say came through him?
questions.answer: It says he brought lofty branches of knowledge and uncovered Divine knowledge.

questions.question: What is the first major truth these scholars strongly confirm together?
questions.answer: They strongly confirm the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: How is the oneness of Allah connected to the Prophet’s mission in the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as the base and main foundation of his mission.

questions.question: What else do these scholars agree about besides Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: They agree that the Prophet is truthful and that his words are true.

questions.question: How strong does the passage say their proof is?
questions.answer: It says their proof is extremely clear, like bright daylight.

questions.question: What work is named near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Risale-i Nur in relation to the Prophet’s truthfulness?
questions.answer: It says even that work, with its many parts, serves as one proof of his truthfulness.

questions.question: What qualities are given for the scholars and sages mentioned here?
questions.answer: They are described as pure, sincere, careful, faithful, and highly learned.

questions.question: Did these people gain their highest knowledge by ignoring the Prophet’s message or by learning from it?
questions.answer: They gained it by learning from his message.

questions.question: Why is the Prophet’s unlettered state important in this passage?
questions.answer: It makes his bringing such deep truth and knowledge even more amazing.

questions.question: According to the passage, what did he bring that helped produce top-level scholars?
questions.answer: He brought sacred truths, great sciences, and knowledge from Allah.

questions.question: What belief is called the foundation of his mission?
questions.answer: Belief in the unity of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say these scholars do with strong proofs?
questions.answer: They prove and confirm Allah’s oneness and also witness to the Prophet’s truthfulness.

questions.question: What comparison is used to show how obvious this proof is?
questions.answer: It is compared to daylight.

questions.question: How is the Risale-i Nur described in number?
questions.answer: It is described as having one hundred parts.

questions.question: Even though it has many parts, how is the Risale-i Nur counted in this argument?
questions.answer: It is counted as a single proof supporting the Prophet’s truthfulness.

questions.question: Which group of people is used in this passage as evidence for the Prophet’s truthfulness?
questions.answer: Highly trained scholars and faithful sages are used as evidence.

questions.question: What do their lives show about the effect of the Prophet’s teachings?
questions.answer: Their lives show that his teachings can raise people to the highest levels of learning.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that these scholars are morally trustworthy?
questions.answer: They are described as sincere, purified, careful, and faithful.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Prophet’s teachings to advanced knowledge?
questions.answer: It says that through his teachings people reached great learning, and that he brought lofty sciences and Divine knowledge.

questions.question: What is the first testimony given by these scholars?
questions.answer: Their first testimony is to the unity of Allah.

questions.question: What is the second testimony they give?
questions.answer: Their second testimony is that the Prophet is truthful and his speech is true.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about disagreement among them on this issue?
questions.answer: It suggests that there is no disagreement because they are united in their witness.

questions.question: How clear is their witness said to be?
questions.answer: It is said to be as clear as daytime light.

questions.question: What example from later scholarship is added at the end?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is added as an example.

questions.question: Why is mentioning the Risale-i Nur helpful to the argument in the passage?
questions.answer: It gives an additional example of learned proof pointing to the Prophet’s truthfulness.

questions.question: In this passage, what do great scholars and sages agree about?
questions.answer: They agree about Allah’s oneness and the truthfulness of the Prophet.

questions.question: What kind of educational path led them to the highest rank of knowledge?
questions.answer: They followed the teaching and training contained in the truths brought by the Prophet.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the truths he brought?
questions.answer: It presents them as sacred truths.

questions.question: What does the passage say he brought even though he was unlettered?
questions.answer: He brought elevated sciences and discovered Divine knowledge.

questions.question: What does this contrast between being unlettered and bringing deep knowledge help the reader notice?
questions.answer: It helps the reader notice the extraordinary nature of his mission.

questions.question: Which central belief stands at the base of his mission?
questions.answer: The oneness of Allah stands at its base.

questions.question: Do the scholars merely believe this privately, or do they also support it with evidence?
questions.answer: They also support it with very strong evidence.

questions.question: What do they testify about the Prophet himself?
questions.answer: They testify that he is a true teacher and that what he says is true.

questions.question: What image is used to show the strength and brightness of this proof?
questions.answer: The image of daylight is used.

questions.question: What book is mentioned as another proof?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying that its many sections still count as one proof?
questions.answer: It means the whole work together forms one united witness to his truthfulness.

questions.question: What is the passage trying to prove by mentioning millions of scholars and sages?
questions.answer: It is trying to prove that the Prophet’s message is true and trustworthy.

questions.question: What personal qualities make their witness stronger?
questions.answer: Their sincerity, purity, carefulness, faith, and high learning make it stronger.

questions.question: How did they arrive at the highest level of knowledge according to the passage?
questions.answer: They arrived there by studying and following the teachings brought by the Prophet.

questions.question: What unusual fact about the Prophet increases the force of the argument?
questions.answer: He did not have formal literacy, yet such great knowledge came through him.

questions.question: Name one kind of knowledge the passage says he brought.
questions.answer: He brought sacred truths, or lofty sciences, or Divine knowledge.

questions.question: What basic truth about Allah do these scholars prove together?
questions.answer: They prove that Allah is One.

questions.question: After proving Allah’s oneness, what do they say about the Prophet?
questions.answer: They say he is truthful and that his words are true.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the clearness of this evidence?
questions.answer: It describes it as obvious like broad daylight.

questions.question: What later work is mentioned by name?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is mentioned.

questions.question: How is that work related to the argument of this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as one more proof supporting the Prophet’s truthfulness.

questions.question: According to this passage, who learned from the Prophet’s teachings and rose to the highest rank of knowledge?
questions.answer: Vast numbers of sincere scholars and faithful sages did.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s formal education?
questions.answer: It says he was unlettered.

questions.question: Even without that kind of schooling, what came through him?
questions.answer: Sacred truths, high forms of knowledge, and knowledge connected to Allah came through him.

questions.question: What belief is described as the foundation of his mission?
questions.answer: The belief that Allah is One.

questions.question: How do the scholars relate to that belief?
questions.answer: They confirm and prove it together with very strong evidence.

questions.question: What do they also confirm about the Prophet as a person and messenger?
questions.answer: They confirm that he is truthful and that what he says is true.

questions.question: What word shows that these scholars are united in their testimony?
questions.answer: The passage shows this with the idea that they are unanimous.

questions.question: What titles for the Prophet show his role in teaching others?
questions.answer: He is called a supreme teacher and a great master.

questions.question: What does the daylight comparison teach the reader about this proof?
questions.answer: It teaches that the proof is plain, bright, and hard to deny.

questions.question: What large work is mentioned near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur with one hundred parts.

questions.question: What role does that work play in the final sentence of the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as a single additional proof of the Prophet’s truthfulness.
